name: arXiv API id_list responses for the 16 paper records found duplicated under two slugs
notes:
THE IDENTIFIER EVIDENCE for the duplicate-slug consolidation. Every arXiv ID involved in a same-paper/slug-different pair was re-fetched from the arXiv API on 2026-10-05 in three id_list batches, per the rule that no arXiv ID in this repo is ever written from memory. Four separate queries were issued, covering 16 papers in the duplicate pairs plus RAPID, MegaScale-Infer and six wave-4 records.
WHAT THE API CONFIRMED, one entry per duplicate pair, with title and author list as returned: 2111.00396 'Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces' (Gu, Goel, Re); 2311.18677 'Splitwise: Efficient generative LLM inference using phase splitting' (Patel, Choukse, Zhang, Shah, Goiri, Maleki, Bianchini); 2312.07104 'SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs' (Zheng, Yin, Xie, Sun, Huang, Yu, Cao, Kozyrakis, Stoica, Gonzalez, Barrett, Sheng); 2310.03294 'DISTFLASHATTN: Distributed Memory-efficient Attention for Long-context LLMs Training' (Li, Shao, Xie, Xing, Ma, Stoica, Gonzalez, Zhang); 2302.10866 'Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models' (Poli, Massaroli, Nguyen, Fu, Dao, Baccus, Bengio, Ermon, Re); 2405.21060 'Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality' (Dao, Gu); 2307.08621 'Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models' (Sun, Dong, Huang, Ma, Xia, Xue, Wang, Wei); 2305.13048 'RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era' (Peng, Alcaide, Anthony, Albalak, ... 33 authors); 2501.00663 'Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time' (Behrouz, Zhong, Mirrokni); 2402.18668 'Simple linear attention language models balance the recall-throughput tradeoff' (Arora, Eyuboglu, Zhang, Timalsina, Alberti, Zinsley, Zou, Rudra, Re); 2510.26692 'Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture' (Kimi Team, ...); 2404.07143 'Leave No Context Behind: Efficient Infinite Context Transformers with Infini-attention' (Munkhdalai, Faruqui, Gopal); 2401.04658 'Lightning Attention-2: A Free Lunch for Handling Unlimited Sequence Lengths in Large Language Models' (Qin, Sun, Li, Shen, Sun, Zhong); 2405.04434 'DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model'; 2412.19437 'DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report'; 2312.00752 'Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces' (Gu, Dao).
TWO ID CORRECTIONS FELL OUT OF THIS, both of which are title-collision near-misses that would have passed a name check: the paper actually titled 'Various Lengths, Constant Speed: Efficient Language Modeling with Lightning Attention' is arXiv 2405.17381 and is a DIFFERENT paper from 'Lightning Attention-2' (2401.04658), and it is the one that was published at ICML 2024 - so 2401.04658 must NOT inherit an ICML venue from a search that found 2405.17381. Second, 2401.04658's real title ends 'in Large Language Models', not 'in Linear Attention', which is the shorter form the repo's records carry and which does not match the arXiv title.
TWO AFFILIATION BLOCKS ALSO CAME FROM THE SAME QUERY SET via the arXiv HTML full text, and both contradict a repo record: 2401.04658's byline carries 'OpenNLPLab' for all six authors and names NO university, and 2302.10866's byline carries '1Stanford University' and '2Mila and Universite de Montreal' and names neither CMU nor NVIDIA.
